# Godance

> OpenAI-compatible REST API that routes to 15+ AI providers across text, image, and
> video — drop-in for chat; images support jobs or sync-key responses, and video uses jobs. One credit ledger, one
> billing line, one SDK. Pay with card, ACH, SEPA, or USDT. Pass-through provider pricing
> plus a platform fee (5% text, 12% image, 10–15% video) — no tiers, no seats, no
> subscriptions.

## Positioning

- vs. OpenRouter: Godance covers image and video too, not just text.
- vs. Eden AI: no account tiers — one published fee per model (Eden's fee is tier-dependent).
- vs. Fireworks / Together: pure aggregator — no GPUs, no model weights, no lock-in.
- vs. B.AI / WorldClaw: built for people building with AI, whether or not they are engineers
  yet — work out a prompt in the Studio, keep it as a recipe, then run it at scale through
  the same OpenAI-compatible API.

## For AI assistants writing code

- Complete reference, one file: every route with a runnable curl example and a Python
  example, using the real field names — https://godance.ai/llms-full.txt
- OpenAPI 3.1 description of every route, for tools — https://api.godance.ai/v1/openapi.yaml
- Without code: two n8n templates that run a Google Sheet's rows as Godance image or video
  jobs — https://github.com/GoDanceAi/godance/tree/main/integrations/n8n
- From inside an AI assistant (Claude Code, Cursor, any MCP client): the same API as MCP tools
  at https://api.godance.ai/mcp, with the same key and caps; every tool that spends takes
  max_cost_cents — https://godance.ai/docs/#mcp


Workflow and conditional capabilities:
- Studio: open /create/image or /create/video in the app; select compatible jobs in /history to compare. Keep a setup in /recipes and run a version over rows in /batches. Run at scale provides code, assistant prompts and n8n options. These page visits start no paid job.
- Image inputs require operator enablement, adult eligibility, accepted input terms and a capable model. Audio and embeddings are not implemented. Video BYOK and unsupported video remix/edit/extension operations are not live.
- Provider keys are conditional on configured support and account/provider status, not an enterprise tier: use Settings → Provider keys or the existing provider-credentials API. Regional restrictions still apply; an existing unsupported credential remains manageable.
- Community requires backend/account permission and moderated approved content: profiles, recipe publishing and follows use signed-in session routes, not API keys. Public read routes expose only approved content. See https://godance.ai/docs/#community-workflow.
- User routing policies are API-only and conditional on operator enablement/account allowlisting. See https://godance.ai/docs/#routing-policies and the OpenAPI schema; there is no app policy editor.
- MCP setup is under API keys → Use with MCP, authenticated with an API key. A setup link does not assert backend or provider health. See https://godance.ai/docs/#mcp and https://godance.ai/docs/#n8n.
- Self-hosting instructions and configuration reference: https://github.com/GoDanceAi/godance/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md. Deployment and optional capability activation are separate operator decisions.

## API surface (OpenAI-compatible)

- POST /v1/chat/completions — streaming + non-streaming
- POST /v1/images/generations — async (202 + job_id) when the model is flagged
  requires_async in /v1/models (currently every image model) or the request sets
  async:true; otherwise sync. An API key set to image_response "sync" gets the images
  in the response instead (see "Images with the OpenAI SDK" below)
- POST /v1/videos/generations — async only, signed webhook callback
- POST /v1/videos, GET /v1/videos, GET /v1/videos/{id}, GET /v1/videos/{id}/content,
  DELETE /v1/videos/{id} — the same video jobs in the shape of OpenAI's Videos API, so
  OpenAI SDK video code works (see "Video with the OpenAI SDK" below)
- GET /v1/jobs/{id} — status of an async generation, with its prompt and params,
  every output (outputs[]: index, url, contentType, sizeBytes, revisedPrompt; each url
  signed at read time), purged, saved, and mediaExpiresAt (files and prompt deleted 90
  days after creation; null while the job is saved)
- GET /v1/jobs — your jobs, newest first, as a bare array; optional limit (1-100),
  before (a job id: older jobs only), modality (IMAGE | VIDEO), status, saved (true:
  only saved jobs; false: only the others)
- PUT /v1/jobs/{id}/saved, DELETE /v1/jobs/{id}/saved — save a DONE job to keep its
  files and prompt past the 90 days, or un-save it; 204 and idempotent. Saving answers
  409 with code job_not_saveable (not DONE, or files already deleted) or
  saved_limit_reached (an account can save up to 500 jobs). Un-saving puts the 90 days
  back: a job already older than that is deleted at the next nightly clean-up
- GET /v1/jobs/saved — {count, limit}: how many jobs you have saved, and the most you can
- /v1/recipes — keep a prompt template as a recipe with numbered versions: POST creates
  one ({title, modality, template, variables: [{name, default}], model, params}); GET
  lists (limit, before); GET, PATCH {title} and DELETE /v1/recipes/{id}; GET and POST
  /v1/recipes/{id}/versions (POST writes a version only when something changed, else
  200 with the latest). A variable is written {{name}}. Each recipe carries attempts
  and spent_cents. Up to 500 recipes per account and 200 versions per recipe (409
  recipe_limit_reached)
- Run a recipe: on POST /v1/images/generations or /v1/videos/generations send
  recipe: {version_id, variables: {name: value}} in place of prompt (both → 400
  prompt_and_recipe). The filled-in template is the job's prompt and price. The job
  then has recipe: {id, version, variables}; GET /v1/jobs?recipe={id} lists its jobs
- POST /v1/recipe-batches — run one recipe version over up to 500 rows ({version_id,
  rows: [{variables, inputs}], model, params, max_concurrency 1-4, webhook_url}). Each row
  is an ordinary job (channel "BATCH", batch: {id, row}); the batch charges nothing
  itself, and it pauses (it does not fail) when credit or a spending cap runs out:
  POST /v1/recipe-batches/{id}/resume continues it, POST /v1/recipe-batches/{id}/cancel
  skips the rows not started. POST /v1/recipe-batches/estimate prices it first. Two
  unfinished batches per account (409 batch_limit_reached)
- GET /v1/recipe-batches, GET /v1/recipe-batches/{id}, GET /v1/recipe-batches/{id}/rows,
  GET /v1/recipe-batches/{id}/results.csv and GET /v1/recipe-batches/{id}/results.zip —
  your batches, their progress, each row's status with its job and signed output links,
  and the results as files. One signed recipe_batch.completed webhook when a batch ends
- POST /v1/estimates — price of an image or video request before sending it
  ({model, n, size, seconds} → estimated_cost_cents, the exact amount the request would
  reserve); no charge, no job
- GET /v1/models — catalog enumeration; image and video entries may carry
  godance.display_name, godance.description and godance.capabilities (sizes,
  default_size, durations, default_seconds, max_n; a missing key means unknown, a
  missing max_n means 1). An n above max_n answers 400 before any charge
- CRUD /v1/keys — API key management (plaintext returned exactly once); each key has
  image_response, "async" or "sync", set at POST /v1/keys or changed with
  PATCH /v1/keys/{id} {"image_response": "sync"} (signed-in session only). A key can
  also have daily_cap_cents and monthly_cap_cents (the most it may spend in a UTC day
  and month; past one a request answers 402) and expires_at (after it, 401); null means
  none, and a PATCH changes only the fields it sends. GET /v1/keys shows each key's
  spent_today_cents and spent_month_cents
- POST /v1/billing/topup — Stripe Checkout for card / ACH / SEPA
- GET /v1/webhooks/secret — signing secret (Stripe-style HMAC-SHA256)
- POST /v1/webhooks/secret/rotate — rotate with 24h dual-signature grace

## Images with the OpenAI SDK

Standard OpenAI SDK image code works unchanged when the API key's image_response is
"sync": client.images.generate(model="gpt-image-2", prompt="...") waits for the job (up
to about 90 seconds) and returns 200 with OpenAI's created and data, plus job_id and
cost_cents. Read result.data[0].url; GPT Image models also return data[0].b64_json by
default, as OpenAI's API does, and response_format ("url" or "b64_json") selects one.
If the job is still running at the limit the answer is 202 with {job_id, status,
poll_url} and Retry-After: 5, so check for it and poll GET /v1/jobs/{id}. A failed job
answers 502 problem JSON with code "generation_failed" and the charge is refunded. With
an "async" key (the default for keys made before this setting) the answer is always the
202; "async": true in the body or a Prefer: respond-async header asks for that on one
request. Video is always a job. Errors on POST /v1/images/generations and
POST /v1/images/edits are problem JSON that also carries OpenAI's error object, so the
SDK's exceptions carry the message, e.code and e.param. client.images.create_variation
is not supported: POST /v1/images/variations answers 404 image_variations_not_supported.
A bearer token that is not a Godance key (an OpenAI key left in OPENAI_API_KEY) answers
401, and the problem's detail says so.

## Video with the OpenAI SDK

OpenAI SDK video code works with the base URL, the key and the model changed:
video = client.videos.create_and_poll(model="seedance-2.0", prompt="...", seconds="8"),
then client.videos.download_content(video.id, variant="video").write_to_file("out.mp4").
model is a Godance video model and is required: OpenAI shut down its own Videos API and
sora-2 models on 2026-09-24, so do not send "sora-2". A video is a Godance job with the
same id (GET /v1/jobs/{id}); the video object adds cost_cents and job_url. status is
queued, in_progress, completed or failed (error.code "generation_failed", reservation
returned). GET /v1/videos/{id}/content streams the file (variant=video; thumbnail answers
404 because no model stores one). GET /v1/videos lists {data, first_id, last_id, has_more}
(limit, after, order). DELETE /v1/videos/{id} deletes the files now and refunds nothing.
input_reference (an image to start from) is a file part or {"file_id": "..."}; it is part
of image inputs, which answer 403 inputs_disabled until they are switched on. The Godance
extensions last_frame, reference_images, recipe and webhook_url go in extra_body; the
SDK's form carries a nested value as bracketed fields (recipe[version_id]), which Godance
reads back. With a recipe, pass prompt="". A field Godance does not read (n, a typo) is
never dropped: it answers 400 invalid_parameter, and e.param names it. Remix,
edits, extensions and characters are not supported and answer 404 with a code of their
own. Errors on these routes are problem JSON that also carries OpenAI's error object, so
the SDK's exceptions carry the message.

## Models

The live list, with current per-model rates, is GET https://api.godance.ai/v1/models
(public) or https://godance.ai/models. Snapshot as of October 2026:

### Text
- OpenAI: gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-nano, gpt-4.1, gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini
- Anthropic: claude-opus-4-7, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-haiku-4-5,
  claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, claude-3-5-haiku-20241022
- Google Vertex: gemini-3.1-pro, gemini-3.1-flash-lite, gemini-1.5-pro, gemini-1.5-flash
- xAI: grok-4
- DeepSeek: deepseek-v4-pro, deepseek-v4-flash
- Moonshot: kimi-k2.6
- Alibaba: qwen-3.6, qwen-3.6-coder
- Zhipu: glm-4.7-flash
- MiniMax: minimax-m2.7
- Baidu: ernie-5.1
- Volcengine Ark: doubao-1.6-pro

### Image (async — returns a job_id; poll GET /v1/jobs/{id} or use a webhook)
- OpenAI: gpt-image-2, gpt-image-1.5
- Google Vertex: imagen-4, nano-banana
- Black Forest Labs: flux-2-pro, flux-1.1-pro
- Alibaba: qwen-image-2.0, qwen-image-2.0-pro
- Volcengine Ark: seedream-5.0
- Stability: sdxl

### Video (async-only by design — durations 1–5 minutes; HTTP sync would time out)
- OpenAI: sora-2, sora-2-pro, sora-2-pro-hd
- Google Vertex: veo-3.1, veo-3.1-fast
- Volcengine Ark: seedance-2.0
- Kling: kling-3.0
- Runway: runway-gen4
- MiniMax: minimax-hailuo-2.3

## Pricing

Provider list price plus a platform fee: 5% on text, 12% on images, and 10–15% on video
depending on the model. No tiers, no seats, no minimums. Top up the ledger; spend across
every model.

- Per-model fee: the markup_percent field on each entry in GET /v1/models
- Per-model rates: https://godance.ai/models
- Pricing page: https://godance.ai/pricing

## Deployment

Two-region: DigitalOcean primary (NYC3 / FRA1), Alibaba Cloud secondary (HK / SG) for
disaster recovery and low-latency to Chinese model providers. DNS-level failover via
Cloudflare health checks on /healthz.

Per-region provider allowlist enforced in code. The Alicloud region routes only DeepSeek,
Moonshot (Kimi), Alibaba (Qwen), Zhipu (GLM), MiniMax, Baidu (ERNIE), Kling, and
Volcengine Ark (Doubao / Seedream / Seedance). Western providers (OpenAI, Anthropic,
Google Vertex, xAI, BFL Flux, Stability, Runway) never route through Alicloud —
compliance with upstream terms of service for Chinese-hosted infrastructure.

## Fallback chains

Configure per-model fallbacks (e.g. claude-3-5-sonnet → claude-3-5-haiku → gpt-4o).
On primary 5xx / timeout / 429, Godance transparently retries the next entry. Response
carries fallback_used:true. Each fallback re-checks the regional allowlist.

## Webhook signing

Header: X-Godance-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>[,v1=<hex>...]

Multiple v1=... entries appear during the 24-hour grace window after a secret rotation.
Verifiers walk all v1 entries and accept the request if ANY matches the stored secret
(Stripe-compatible pattern). Per-user secret retrievable via GET /v1/webhooks/secret;
rotate via POST /v1/webhooks/secret/rotate.

## Status

Real-time per-provider availability and latency:
https://godance.ai/status (launches with public beta)
